stem.en: Kabir asks why a leaf "does not just absorb every colour and be black, since black absorbs the most". Set that question aside; it returns in three lessons. For now: a photon of green light hits a chlorophyll. What happens?

text.en: It passes through or bounces off. Green's energy matches no gap between chlorophyll's rungs, so no electron is lifted. The photon leaves, which is why you see it.
It is absorbed and lifts an electron a little way.

feedback.en: Electrons take whole rungs or nothing, from I.3. A photon that fits no rung is not absorbed at all.

text.en: It is absorbed and turned into heat.

feedback.en: A leaf does warm in the sun, but green photons mostly leave it. That is the whole reason it looks green.

text.en: It is absorbed and lifts two electrons half way.

feedback.en: One photon lifts one electron one whole rung. There is no half.

explanation.en: A photon is a packet, from I.3. It is absorbed only if its energy equals a gap. Chlorophyll's gaps are red-sized and blue-sized. Green fits nowhere.
